evidence.title: Starbucks faces lawsuit over 'sugar-free' protein drinks

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks statement to Reuters
occurrences.quote_span: "We believe these claims have no merit," the company told Reuters.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks menus, marketing materials, website and app
occurrences.quote_span: Starbucks said it has consistently provided information about the beverages, including their nutritional content, through its menus, marketing materials, website and app.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint and applicable state consumer-protection laws
occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit seeks monetary damages for consumers who bought the beverages and alleges Starbucks violated state laws protecting customers from false or misleading advertising.
occurrences.speaker: the lawsuit's plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Applicable federal food-labeling regulations and the lawsuit complaint
occurrences.quote_span: Federal regulations cited in the complaint prohibit using "sugar-free" on beverages containing more than 0.5 grams of sugar per 12-ounce serving, according to the lawsuit.
occurrences.speaker: the lawsuit
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint
occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit names eight beverages in Starbucks' protein line:
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint
occurrences.quote_span: The plaintiffs also want Starbucks to stop calling the drinks "sugar-free" if they contain sugar.
occurrences.speaker: the plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint and applicable labeling requirements
occurrences.quote_span: The plaintiffs also allege Starbucks failed to provide required disclaimers stating the drinks are not low-calorie foods or intended for weight control.
occurrences.speaker: the plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint filed in federal court in Seattle
occurrences.quote_span: Starbucks is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit from consumers who accuse the coffee chain of falsely advertising eight protein beverages as "sugar-free" even though they allegedly contain 13 to 21 grams of sugar.
occurrences.speaker: the consumers who filed the lawsuit
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks ingredient lists and beverage preparation specifications
occurrences.quote_span: Starbucks said it does not add sugar to the beverages and uses sugar-free syrup for flavoring.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Federal court filing docket and complaint in Seattle
occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit, filed Oct. 2 in federal court in Seattle, alleges the drinks contain lactose, a naturally occurring sugar in milk.
occurrences.speaker: the lawsuit's plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint and Starbucks nutrition information
occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit alleges the beverages contain 13 to 21 grams of sugar per 20- or 24-ounce venti serving.
occurrences.speaker: the lawsuit's plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint
occurrences.quote_span:
The lawsuit names eight beverages in Starbucks' protein line:
- Sugar-Free Vanilla Protein Latte
- Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Latte
- Sugar-Free Vanilla Protein Matcha
- Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha
- Iced Sugar-Free Vanilla Protein Latte
- Iced Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Latte
- Iced Sugar-Free Vanilla Protein Matcha
- Iced Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks ingredient and nutrition records
occurrences.quote_span: The company said the sugar comes from the protein-boosted milk used in the drinks.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks product webpage for Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha
occurrences.quote_span: The product is described as having "No Added Sugar."
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks' website
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks' statement regarding the lawsuit
occurrences.quote_span: Starbucks disputes the allegations and said it intends to defend itself.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: USA TODAY reporter contact records and responses
occurrences.quote_span: USA TODAY contacted Starbucks and the plaintiffs' attorneys on Oct. 6 for additional comment on the lawsuit and its allegations, but did not receive an immediate response.
occurrences.speaker: USA TODAY
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks website nutrition listings for Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha
occurrences.quote_span: For example, Starbucks' website lists 16 grams of sugar in a 16-ounce Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha and 21 grams in a 20-ounce version.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks' website
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint
occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit alleges Starbucks' use of "sugar-free" could mislead consumers who are trying to reduce their sugar intake.
occurrences.speaker: the plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: The proposed class-action complaint
occurrences.quote_span: The plaintiffs argue consumers would not reasonably expect beverages with "sugar-free" in their names to contain that much sugar.
occurrences.speaker: the plaintiffs
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks' statement regarding the lawsuit
occurrences.quote_span: Starbucks disputes the allegations and said it intends to defend itself.
occurrences.speaker: Starbucks
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit

occurrences.checkable_against: Starbucks menu launch records and Back to Starbucks product announcements
occurrences.quote_span: Starbucks introduced the protein beverages in September 2025 as part of its "Back to Starbucks" updated menu.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Starbucks sugar-free protein drinks labeling lawsuit
